summary: Title: Ripple adds Stripe-owned wallets to XRP Ledger as AI payments pass 14 million URL Source: https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/10/14/ripple-adds-stripe-owned-wallets-to-xrp-ledger-as-ai-payments-pass-14-million Published Time: 2026-10-14T05:24:12.159Z Markdown Content: Oct 14, 2026, 1:24 a.m. EDT 3 min read ![Image 1: Brad Garlinghouse, the CEO of Ripple Labs (Jesse Hamilton/CoinDesk)](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2F260b57a4fe560b018cc5f2eb91b9df196b57dc92-3773x2122.jpg%3Frect%3D1%2C0%2C3772%2C2122%26w%3D1920%26h%3D1080%26auto%3Dformat&w=1200&q=75) Brad Garlinghouse, the CEO of Ripple Labs (Jesse Hamilton/CoinDesk) Summary * Ripple and Stripe-owned Privy are partnering to let developers embed XRP Ledger wallets in payments apps, allowing customers to transfer XRP, the RLUSD stablecoin and other assets without setting up separate crypto wallets. * The integration could also enable AI agents to hold funds and automatically pay for online data and services, with a Ripple executive saying such payments account for about 25 percent of XRP Ledger activity. * Embedded wallets will still require funding to become active because each new XRP Ledger account must receive the network’s minimum reserve of 1 XRP, even if it will be used only for stablecoin payments. Ripple is bringing wallet technology from Stripe-owned Privy to the XRP Ledger, allowing financial applications and AI agents to create accounts, hold cryptocurrencies and make payments without requiring users to manage their own wallet software. The move will allow developers to create wallets inside their products and authorize transfers involving XRP, Ripple’s dollar-pegged RLUSD stablecoin and other assets issued on the network, per a release shared with CoinDesk. Coins.ph, the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the Philippines, is facing punitive action from financial regulators at the country’s central bank, two people with knowledge of the situation said. The infractions, which are said to involve serving offshore gambling firms, are serious enough for the 12-year-old company to be stripped of its license to operate, which would cause “an earthquake” in the Philippines’ crypto ecosystem, according to one of the people. The exchange, which has over 18 million customers, has a 24-hour spot trading volume of about $50 million and controls some 75%-80% of peso-to-stablecoin liquidity in the Philippines, a key transaction in the world's fourth-largest remittance recipient.
